findings.title: Online action reducers capture a stale session snapshot across an await and overwrite the whole store with .set(), silently discarding concurrent mutations
findings.description: addExercise() captures `const session = get(state.currentSession)` at line 106, then performs network awaits, and at line 211 rebuilds the whole store with `state.currentSession.set({ ...session, exercises: [...session.exercises, newExercise] })` using that stale pre-await snapshot. The same stale-snapshot-then-.set pattern appears in addSet online (sets.ts:163 -> sets.ts:204), markExerciseDone online (sets.ts:98 -> sets.ts:135), and removeExercise online (core.ts:245 -> core.ts:271). replaceExerciseSets (sets.ts:73) does it correctly with .update(); these reducers do not. Any mutation applied to currentSession between the snapshot and the .set is overwritten and lost. addExercise is the concretely reachable case: its FIRST await, loadLastTimeForExercise() at line 118, runs BEFORE state.loading.set(true) at line 179, so the UI (SessionExercise disabled={$loading} in routes/+page.svelte:225) is NOT disabled during that network round-trip and the user can freely edit existing exercises.
findings.attackOrTrigger: Online. User types a brand-new exercise name (not in recentSessions cache and not yet in lastTimeByExercise) and taps add. addExercise awaits loadLastTimeForExercise() over the network (~100ms+) while loading is still false and nothing is disabled. During that window the user edits an existing exercise's notes / a setting / tracking (updateExerciseNotes etc. in settings.ts synchronously .set the store) or logs a set. When createExercise resolves, core.ts:211 does .set({...stale session}) and wipes that edit out of currentSession. For debounce-synced fields (notes/settings/tracking) the loss is permanent: their 650ms debounced backend push, syncExercise() at settings.ts:45-66, reads get(state.currentSession) at fire time (settings.ts:47), which is now the clobbered snapshot, so it persists the OLD value to the backend and the edit is gone even after reload.
findings.why: A logged set or an exercise-notes/settings edit silently vanishes from the live in-progress session; for debounce-synced fields it is written back to the backend as the old value, so the user's data is permanently lost, not just visually. The user sees their edit disappear mid-workout and is likely to re-enter it, which then races/duplicates.
findings.fixSketch: In every online reducer, do not build the next session from the pre-await snapshot. After the await, use state.currentSession.update((current) => ...) and merge into `current` (the live state), exactly as replaceExerciseSets already does at sets.ts:73-81. Also move loading.set(true) (or otherwise gate input) to before the first network await in addExercise so the pre-load fetch does not run with the UI live.

findings.title: Network failure during the final endWorkout of submitEndSession drops the entered mood/notes and leaves the workout un-ended forever on the next sync
findings.description: In submitEndSession online path, exercises are ended via Promise.all (session.ts:309) and then endWorkout is awaited (session.ts:330). If connectivity drops specifically during endWorkout, the catch at session.ts:345-352 treats it as a network failure and calls persistInProgressSession(state), which saves the offline record with status 'in_progress' and NO end_mood / end_notes / endedAt (offline.ts:97-108). Contrast the offline branch (session.ts:291-301) which saves status 'pending_sync' WITH end_mood and endedAt. On reconnect, syncOne only calls endWorkout when `record.status === 'pending_sync' && record.end_mood && record.session.endedAt` (offline.ts:269); for a positive-id in_progress record it replays the exercises and then just deletes the record at offline.ts:283-285 without ever ending the workout.
findings.attackOrTrigger: Online, user opens the end-session modal, picks a mood and notes, taps End. endExercise calls succeed, then endWorkout fails with a network error. App flips to offline and persists an in_progress record with no mood. On reconnect syncOne finishes the exercises and deletes the record without calling endWorkout. The workout stays active on the server and the mood/notes the user typed are gone.
findings.why: The user believes they finished and rated their workout, but the session is never actually ended on the backend and their end-of-session mood/notes are silently discarded. They must notice the session is still 'in progress' and end it again.
findings.fixSketch: In the submitEndSession network-failure catch, persist an end record analogous to the offline branch: status 'pending_sync' with end_mood, end_notes and session.endedAt set, so syncOne's endWorkout branch (offline.ts:269) fires on reconnect. Apply endedAt/mood to the session object before persisting.

findings.title: Turning off split-weight with unequal left/right silently rewrites the logged weight to max(left,right), changing the recorded set and volume
findings.description: toggleExerciseSplitWeight(enabled=false) collapses each set's two side weights into a single weight using Math.max(left, right) at weightModes.ts:138, then persists those sets via replaceSets. For an exercise with per-side weight still on (perSideWeight true, splitWeight now false), calculateExerciseVolumeKg treats the single weight as per-side and doubles it (metrics.ts:20-21: reps * weight * 2). So a set logged as left=40/right=60 (volume reps*100) becomes weight=60 (volume reps*120) after the toggle. The lighter side is discarded and total volume is inflated, and the change is pushed to the backend.
findings.attackOrTrigger: During a live workout the user logs a dumbbell exercise with different left/right loads while split-weight is on, then toggles split-weight off. Every asymmetric set is rewritten to the heavier side and the volume for that exercise jumps.
findings.why: The user's actually-lifted weights are silently altered and their session volume is mis-computed; the corrupted values are persisted to the backend.
findings.fixSketch: Preserve volume when collapsing sides, e.g. weight = (left + right) / 2 rather than Math.max, or surface a confirmation that turning off split-weight will replace both sides with a single value.
